title: Recipe 59 — Model resilience & cost (failover, budgets, and right-sizing)

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “Four escalating answers to 'the model failed or cost too much' — each one a few lines of spec.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — nothing committed is touched by a take.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env for the run and scan beats.

beats.label: Type the failover spec
beats.cue: “model_fallbacks: a chain, not a try/catch. When the breaker opens, turns retry down the chain instead of dying.”

beats.label: Lint it
beats.cue: “Clean — failover is declared, so a reviewer sees it in the diff.”

beats.label: Compile it and check it
beats.cue: “--check: GREEN. The chain survives a real install and boot.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok; install ok; boot gated at the provider credentials gate

beats.label: Type the failure taxonomy
beats.cue: “Not every failure should fail over. A 400 is your bug; a 529 is theirs — only one of those deserves a retry.”

beats.label: Read it
beats.cue: “Classifying the failure is what makes the retry safe.”

beats.label: Blank the scratch spec
beats.cue: “Now the far end of the recipe — a pool the router learns over, instead of a fixed chain.”

beats.label: Type the adaptive pool spec
beats.cue: “Candidates with tags — balanced and strong. The router picks per turn, and learns which one was worth it.”

beats.label: Lint it
beats.cue: “Clean. A learned router is still a declared router.”

beats.label: Compile it and check it
beats.cue: “--check: GREEN, gated at the model credential.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok; install ok; boot gated at the provider credentials gate

beats.label: Ask the router what it has learned
beats.cue: “No routing data yet — it says so instead of showing you a confident empty table.”

verify.note: reports honestly with no routing history

beats.label: Read it
beats.cue: “Per-band arms and the current best. After a few hundred turns this is where the savings show up.”

groups.title: Beat 3 · is the cheap model good enough?

beats.label: Read the right-size contract
beats.cue: “right-size answers the question with the dataset instead of a hunch: can the cheap model hold the score?”

beats.label: Read it
beats.cue: “It needs a dataset. Every cost claim in this recipe is measured, never asserted.”

beats.label: Read the model-scan contract
beats.cue: “model-scan runs the whole candidate set and hands you the score/cost frontier.”

beats.label: Read it
beats.cue: “Pick the knee of the curve, not the top of it.”

groups.title: One more thing · budgets and pricing

beats.label: Cap a run
beats.cue: [needs-key] “--budget-usd 2.00 is the hard stop. It ends the run cleanly rather than halfway through a tool call.”

verify.note: interactive REPL bounded by a spend cap; needs a model credential

beats.label: Flag unpriced models
beats.cue: “doctor --models catches a model your pricing table has never heard of — the one that makes every cost number a lie.”

verify.note: flags any model with no pricing row

beats.label: Read it
beats.cue: “If this is empty, your cost dashboard means something. If it isn't, it doesn't.”
